title: Dogfood Roadmap (cross-run trajectory layer)
description: F-fe05c6d7 (wave 39, Feature Pass T1): the canonical contract for the compiled artifact `swarm roadmap compile <run-id>` writes to dogfood/roadmap/<run-id>.json. Per docs/trajectory-and-closure.dispatch.md T1 ('The roadmap is compiled, never authored'), every section here is a QUERY result executed against the control-plane DB and git at compile time — never hand-edited prose, with the single exception of operator_notes (T3), the one human-authored section. This is a swarm-internal envelope, exactly like agent-output.schema.json and case-file.schema.json before it — NOT one of the eight contract-spine payload schemas registered in allSchemas / validatePayload / SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSIONS (that registry gates the record/recordSubmission/finding/pattern/recommendation/doctrine/policy/scenario family). It resolves via this package's existing "./json/*": "./src/json/*" subpath export with a LOCAL Ajv instance in the consuming package, mirroring packages/dogfood-swarm/lib/templates.js:73's require.resolve('@dogfood-lab/schemas/json/agent-output.schema.json') precedent — no new export wiring, and no schema_version value gate. Every array/object section below is REQUIRED even when empty (an empty array or a zero-count object is valid) so an absent key can only ever mean 'the compiler did not run this query,' never 'ran it and found nothing' — a reader is never left guessing which. See $defs.latestPointer for the companion micro-shape of dogfood/roadmap/latest.json (T5), a separate file this same schema also shapes via $ref.
$comment: WAVE-41 SEAM DECISIONS (F-c7b0f47b; coordinator's binding call for this wave: 'the schema is the contract' — core's lib-compiler and verbs' commands/roadmap.js conform their emitters to this document in their own worktrees this same wave, not the reverse). Four things changed HERE, deliberately, in response to the real committed artifact failing this schema with 16 Ajv errors: (1) `sections` stays UNBLESSED — additionalProperties:false already rejected it before this wave and continues to; what changed is that the rejection is now a stated decision, not an accident nobody had looked at. `sections` wholesale-duplicated compile.js's raw internal shape (findings-with-severity/category, a second, INCOMPATIBLE `attention.top[].factors` shape sitting alongside this schema's own `attention.items[].components`, a two-halves drain_queue with yet another shape) that the sections below already contract for in a considered form. Emitters MUST NOT write `sections` into a committed artifact; any richer per-item detail it carried belongs as optional enrichment of the fields below, never a parallel undifferentiated copy. (2) `notesPath` is now an explicit, OPTIONAL, repo-relative-only property (see its own entry below) — this key's mere presence was previously one of the 16 Ajv errors (a disallowed additionalProperty), and a real compile had already committed it as a machine-absolute Windows path, baking one operator's local checkout into version-controlled history (the finding's own first proven exhibit). (3) `compiled_at`'s description was rewritten for honesty about its DB-derived, not wall-clock, semantics; the field NAME is unchanged (see its own entry below). (4) `content_hash` stays OPTIONAL, not promoted to required, with its self-exclusion hashing semantics now specified (see its own entry below). NOT touched by this wave: open_summary / grandfathered_drain / recurrence_stats / attention / operator_notes / drain_queue keep their existing T1-T6 shapes; conforming emitters to THOSE is core's and verbs' materially larger burden, and out of this package's domain to make or verify — packages/dogfood-swarm's own pinned tests (F-1cd5de59, F-74ba2c79) currently assert a flatter, differently-shaped `drain`/`notes`/`expired` CLI surface than this schema's `drain_queue`/`operator_notes`, which core/verbs must reconcile (by conforming the emitter AND, if those tests are asserting a superseded shape, updating them) as part of landing this wave's fix — not something this package can resolve by editing files outside its own domain.

run_id.description: The swarm control-plane run id this roadmap was compiled from (e.g. swarm-1784091637-5127) — NOT a dogfood-record run_id, which names a different identifier namespace (a consumer's own CI run). Charset is constrained because run_id becomes a filesystem path segment (dogfood/roadmap/<run_id>.json), mirroring dogfood-record.schema.json's run_id field and its stated rationale exactly.

sequence.description: T5: increments on a same-run recompile; never edits a prior version. The first compile for a run is sequence 1. A recompile within the same run supersedes with a new sequence number — history is never rewritten. dogfood/roadmap/latest.json (see $defs.latestPointer) is the one mutable indirection that tracks which sequence is newest.

compiled_at.description: WAVE-41 HONESTY FIX (F-c7b0f47b): this is deliberately NOT the wall-clock moment `swarm roadmap compile` was invoked — an earlier version of this description mischaracterized it as exactly that, which was false and has been corrected. The value is sourced from the compiled run's own DB row (`runs.created_at`), held fixed for that run's lifetime, so that two separate compile invocations against byte-identical DB state produce a byte-identical artifact — T1's determinism promise, proven cross-process by F-feeaef78 (see commands/roadmap.js's deterministicNow()). Two compiles of the SAME run, issued minutes or days apart, MUST carry the identical value here by construction; a future implementation that instead stamps a live clock read at invocation time is the regression F-feeaef78 exists to catch, not a more accurate timestamp. Distinct from any per-entry timestamp inside the sections below (e.g. drain_queue[].added_at), which are independently DB-sourced values, not derived from this run-creation stand-in.

repo.description: Full org/repo the roadmap was compiled for. Same pattern as dogfood-finding.schema.json's repo field.

compiled_from.description: The git state the compile queries ran against — the 'and git alone' half of T1's 'compiled from the control-plane DB and git alone.'

commit_sha.description: Full 40-hex commit SHA checked out at compile time. Same pattern as dogfood-record.schema.json's ref.commit_sha.

open_summary.description: T1: 'Factual sections are queries executed at compile time: open/deferred/approved findings' — those three counts are the ones the pass contract names explicitly, and are required. The three optional siblings (fixed/rejected/recurring) round out the full finding-status vocabulary this build recognizes: packages/dogfood-swarm/lib/finding-status.js's CLOSED_FINDING_STATUSES = ['fixed','rejected','deferred'], with 'open'/'approved'/'recurring' all treated as still-open by that module's isOpenFinding(). additionalProperties:false because this is a closed, known status set, not an open-ended bag.

deferred.description: Findings consciously postponed — closed for gate purposes; the deferred ones with provenance/cadence are tracked in drain_queue below.

approved.description: Findings reviewed and greenlit for an amend wave — the DB-canonical work-order findings a run's lanes build against.

recurring.description: Findings reopened via the content-match regression-rediscovery path (a closed finding's fingerprint re-reported) or via C1's evidence-bearing operator reopen.

grandfathered_drain.description: T6 drain state for the frozen grandfathered manifest (the 256-entry migration-debt set referenced in docs/trajectory-and-closure.dispatch.md Q5). frozen_total is the manifest's size at the moment it was frozen (a constant per manifest generation, not recomputed per compile); drained counts entries removed from the manifest by a completed re-review; outstanding lists what remains, each carrying the same per-entry provenance + cadence shape as drain_queue below (Q5: 'unless each entry carries provenance and a re-review cadence' — the failure mode this section exists to avoid is Liargkovas et al. 2023 (arXiv:2311.07482), unaudited suppression-registry debt across 1,425 projects).

frozen_total.description: Size of the grandfathered manifest at the moment it was frozen.

drained.description: Entries removed from the manifest by a completed re-review since freeze.

outstanding.description: Remaining grandfathered entries. Shares $defs/drainEntry with drain_queue so the two sections cannot drift into two different provenance shapes.

recurrence_stats.description: T1: 'recurrence stats (swarm trends internals)'. Deliberately left open (additionalProperties:true) rather than frozen here: the query layer this section reflects (packages/dogfood-swarm/lib/queries/cross-run-analytics.js's queryRecurringFindings and its siblings) is owned by the core/dogfood-swarm domain and evolves independently of this schemas-package registration. Freezing every field here would prematurely couple two domains this pass's own DECOMPOSE_BY_SECRETS scoring (docs/trajectory-and-closure.dispatch.md) deliberately keeps separate. The one field named below is grounded directly in that module's existing return shape as a documented-but-not-exhaustive convention, not a closed contract — an undisclosed gap would itself be the defect (swarms/CLAUDE.md, 'Honesty is a feature of the artifact, not a mood').

top_recurring.description: Fingerprints observed across more than one run, most-recurring first. Mirrors queryRecurringFindings()'s actual return shape (packages/dogfood-swarm/lib/queries/cross-run-analytics.js) rather than redefining it independently.

description.description: A representative description from one of the recurring rows. Not fingerprint-folded — wording may vary run to run; this is a stable pick, not a canonical one.

run_count.description: Distinct runs this fingerprint was observed in. By construction always greater than 1 — that is what makes it 'recurring'.

severity.description: The most severe observation across runs (an explicit rank, not an alphabetical MAX — 'MEDIUM' must not beat 'CRITICAL').

first_seen.description: Earliest run this fingerprint was observed in.

last_seen.description: Most recent run this fingerprint was observed in.

attention.description: T2: a ranked top-K per-file attention list, consumed ONLY as audit-brief context. `advisory` is a non-optional, const-true sibling of the ranked list — structurally inseparable, so a consumer can never read `items` without also validating the label that governs how it may be used.
attention.$comment: T2 is explicit: 'It is never a gate, never a predictor, never auto-blame' (Q3: Lewis et al. 2013, ICSE, research.google/pubs/pub41145 — Google's deployed bug predictor changed no developer behavior; only passive hotspot reports survived. Q3: SZZ-style blame misattributes against developer oracles, Rosa et al. 2021, arXiv:2102.03300). The schema cannot enforce HOW a consumer uses this section — only that the advisory label travels WITH the list and cannot be stripped from an instance without producing a schema violation.

advisory.description: Always true by construction. A compiler cannot emit an attention section without this marker; a consumer cannot read `items` without also seeing this sibling is present and true (T2: 'never a gate, never a predictor, never auto-blame').

items.description: Ranked top-K files by attention score. Empty is valid — no signal this compile.

score.description: Combined attention score — the product of the three normalized components below (T2).

components.description: The three factors T2 names explicitly, each independently sourced: churn relative to file size (Q3: Nagappan & Ball 2005, ICSE — relative, not absolute, churn discriminates); prior-finding recency/count (Q3: Rahman & Devanbu 2013, ICSE — process metrics beat static code metrics); lane-fragmentation, the count of distinct domains that touched the file (Q3: Bird et al. 2011, ESEC/FSE — ownership fragmentation predicts failures better than churn+complexity+coverage combined).

churn.description: Recent churn normalized relative to file size.

recency.description: Prior-finding recency/count signal for this file.

fragmentation.description: Count (or normalized measure) of distinct domains/lanes that have touched this file.

operator_notes.description: T3: the ONLY human-authored section. At most 7 entries (Q1: Shinn et al. 2023, Reflexion, arXiv:2303.11366 — bounded lesson buffers beat unbounded).

expires.description: When this note stops being surfaced by compile. Either an integer horizon (expires after N further runs on this repo) or an ISO-8601 calendar date. Compile MUST drop expired notes LOUDLY — listed in output as EXPIRED, never silently omitted (T3) — but that behavior belongs to the compiler (core domain); this schema only shapes the value, it cannot enforce the drop.

oneOf.description: Expires after this many further runs on this repo.

enforced_by.description: Path to the gate/test that mechanically enforces this note. Required by the conditional below whenever kind='invariant' — 'a lesson without a mechanical verifier is not persisted as a lesson' (Q1: Wang et al. 2023, Voyager, arXiv:2305.16291; Anthropic 2025, Project Vend, anthropic.com/research/project-vend-1 — a long-horizon agent's narrative correction did not hold across days). LIMITATION disclosed up front: this schema can only shape enforced_by as a non-empty string — it cannot verify the referenced gate/test file actually EXISTS on disk. That cross-file existence check belongs to the compiler (core domain), which per this repo's own Class #14 history (scripts/check-finding-regression-pins.mjs's AST-based rebuild after a prose-matching heuristic leaked 7 consecutive audits) should use a real structural check, never a string/regex scan, to confirm enforced_by resolves to something real.

allOf.$comment: T3 invariant-requires-enforced_by conditional — the identical shape to dogfood-finding.schema.json's own proven H4 pattern ('if status==="rejected" then review.reject_reason required'), one file over in this same package. A note claiming kind='invariant' with no mechanical enforcement pointer is exactly the Project Vend failure mode (Q1): a narrative correction that does not hold, because nothing mechanical re-checks it.

drain_queue.description: T6: deferred findings (beyond the grandfathered manifest tracked separately in grandfathered_drain above) with per-entry provenance and re-review cadence. Shares $defs/drainEntry with grandfathered_drain.outstanding so the two sections cannot drift into two different provenance shapes.

content_hash.description: OPTIONAL — WAVE-41 SEAM DECISION (F-c7b0f47b): stays optional, deliberately not promoted to required, even though this wave expects emitters to start populating it. Not part of the locked T1-T6 pass contract (docs/trajectory-and-closure.dispatch.md) — an integrity aid for T5's 'versions supersede, nothing rewrites' discipline, so a consumer can cheaply detect whether a previously-fetched dogfood/roadmap/<run-id>.json has changed, by comparing a freshly computed hash against one it cached earlier. HASHING SEMANTIC (newly specified this wave — the prior text left this undefined, which is why the field was computed by writeRoadmapArtifact but never actually reached the written bytes): if a producer includes this field, it MUST be a hash of the artifact's own serialized bytes computed WITH THIS FIELD ABSENT — hash-then-attach, never hash-including-self, which has no fixed point. Hash algorithm and length remain deliberately unconstrained here: choosing and documenting one is a compiler (core domain) decision, not a schemas-package one. Kept optional rather than required because this schema can only ever enforce the KEY's presence, never the VALUE's correctness — a wrong or stale hash is worse than an absent one, so a producer not yet confident in its self-exclusion computation should omit the field rather than ship a mismatched one. Promoting this to required is a reasonable follow-up once emitters are confirmed to populate it consistently.

notesPath.description: OPTIONAL — WAVE-41 SEAM DECISION (F-c7b0f47b): records which local file compile read the operator-notes seed from. This is compile-ENVIRONMENT provenance, not one of the T1-T6 sections queried from the DB and git themselves — T3 is about note CONTENT, which lives in operator_notes above; this field only says which local file supplied it, and a producer with nothing meaningful to report (e.g. no seed file existed) may omit it entirely. MUST be repo-relative, resolved against the target repo root at read time, never a machine-absolute path baked into a committed artifact. The pattern mechanically enforces this: it rejects a leading `/` or `\`, and a drive-letter prefix such as `C:` or `E:\`. This closes the finding's own first proven exhibit — a real compile had committed this field as a machine-absolute Windows path, which resolves on no checkout but the one that produced it. Before this wave the key was not recognized at all (any value, relative or not, was rejected outright as a disallowed additionalProperty); now a relative value is accepted and only an absolute one is refused, and refused specifically for being absolute rather than merely unrecognized.

drainEntry.description: T6's shared per-entry provenance + cadence shape, used by both grandfathered_drain.outstanding and drain_queue. Every field is required — a drain entry missing an owner or a cadence is exactly the anti-pattern Liargkovas et al. 2023 (arXiv:2311.07482) found across 1,425 projects: suppression registries accumulating as unaudited debt with no forcing function to re-review them (Q5, docs/trajectory-and-closure.dispatch.md).

id.description: Finding id (deferred) or grandfathered-manifest entry id (frozen migration debt).

reason.description: Why this entry is parked here rather than closed outright.

owner.description: Named individual or role accountable for this entry's eventual re-review. Never anonymous — mirrors this repo's NAMED_COMPENSATORS discipline (.claude/rules/workflow-standards.md) applied to drain entries instead of tool calls.

added_at.description: When this entry entered the drain queue.

cadence_runs.description: Re-review cadence, in swarm runs on this repo.

due_at_run.description: The run sequence number at which this entry becomes due for re-review. Compile surfaces entries past this threshold at the top of the next run's digest (T6; Q5's Chromium 'no forcing function is the failure' lesson).

latestPointer.description: T5 companion micro-shape for dogfood/roadmap/latest.json — the ONE mutable pointer to the newest compiled roadmap version for a run. This is a SEPARATE file's contract from the roadmap document above; a consumer validating latest.json directly references it as dogfood-roadmap.schema.json#/$defs/latestPointer, matching the way F-fe05c6d7's own recommendation named it a 'companion micro-shape' rather than a second top-level schema file.

run_id.description: Same run_id as the pointed-to roadmap document.

sequence.description: Same sequence as the pointed-to roadmap document — the newest compiled version for this run.

path.description: Relative path to the versioned roadmap file this pointer resolves to, e.g. dogfood/roadmap/<run_id>.json.
